# Fact ledger: /buyers/gated-communities/ (Gated communities in Myrtle Beach)

Researched 2026-10-13 for batch 2026-10-b, page 2. One row per claim. The writer may use rows marked `verified` only. The researcher filled columns 1 to 7. The verifier fills 8 and 9. Every row is "(added 2026-10-13)".

## Verification summary (2026-10-13)

The verifier did none of the research. Every source below was opened again on 2026-10-13. Beach Pro Team pages were fetched one every 10 seconds (its robots.txt crawl delay). Real Geeks was read through `/property/<MLS#>/` pages only. No Zillow, Realtor.com or Redfin page was opened.

**Counts:** 76 rows. Verified 68. Wrong 4 (rows 25, 44, 48, 56). Unverifiable 4 (rows 52 to 55, Georgetown County: the county server was unreachable).

**Rows the writer may not use as written:** 25 (Pawleys Plantation is not shown gated), 44 (Dye Estates price includes a builder sale), 48 (Waterway Palms price: builder rule applied unevenly; use "about $780,000"), 52 to 55 (Georgetown prices, not re-pulled), 56 (The Reserve price: one deed counted twice).

**What was re-done**

- Gate documents: the Municode text (rows 1 to 3), the Litchfield by the Sea FAQ, guide and barcode form (rows 4 to 7), both Barefoot Resort association pages (rows 8 to 10), the Toll Brothers page (row 11), the Myrtle Trace gate PDF (row 13), and AcclaimWeb index entries 4174/75 and 4786/2971 (rows 15, 16).
- Listings: all 138 listings in the evidence tables were re-read on RE/MAX Southern Shores (gate field, fee, golf field). 99 of them were also re-opened on Beach Pro Team (at least 3 per community; every Grande Dunes listing; every listing quoted in rows 17 to 34), plus 3 Seasons listings for row 14. Counts and fees match the ledger everywhere.
- Prices, Horry County: all 30,339 deeds recorded 10/1/2025 to 9/30/2026 were pulled from AcclaimWeb (same total as the method note), matched to fresh county parcel sets, and the medians and quartiles recomputed. All 153 counted deeds in rows 40 to 50 were opened one by one. The counted lists match. Two exclusion errors are in rows 44 and 48.
- Prices, Georgetown County: not possible (see rows 52 to 56).
- Drive minutes: all 19 OSRM routes (rows 57 to 75) re-run from the named starts; all match. Starts were checked in the county address layer (Horry) or the Census geocoder (Georgetown and two others).
- Gate documents in the deed index: the comments search "GATE" does work (it matches memos that start with GATE). It returns only Seaside Plantation 4174/75, Bellwood Landing 4786/2971 and a private gate and dock easement (4255/25). The researcher's note that a search on "GATE" fails is out of date.

**Per community.** "Gate verified": yes = a document from the association, the builder or the county; partly = only some sections or entrances; listings only = MLS fields and listing directions (seller's agent entered, not the association).

That is 16 communities fully named, 3 named in part (Barefoot, Grande Dunes, Myrtle Trace) and 2 left off (Pawleys Plantation, Indigo Bay). The page keeps at least 8 communities in at least 3 areas.

**Four stretches**

- **Group (which sections are gated).** Barefoot: 8 of 26 neighborhoods labeled; the association also says only "some" townhome communities and low-rise entrances are gated, so an unlabeled neighborhood is not shown ungated. Grande Dunes: the builder ties the staffed gate to Cascadia only; listings are mixed and disagree inside Members Club (2 of 3) and Seville (1 of 2). The 19 Del Webb at Grande Dunes listings show no gate. Tidewater has a "Bluffs side" in one listing's directions. Indigo Bay and Pawleys Plantation: gating is shown for part of the listings only.
- **Time.** Municode is Supplement 88 (the latest). The Litchfield by the Sea guide is the 2026 guide (created 2026-06-25); the commercial form is the 2025 form. The Myrtle Trace policy is a 2025 document. The Seaside rules are from 2019 and the Bellwood policy from 2024, and neither text is posted. Georgetown County dates run to 2026-12-29, so its table cannot be trusted without a deed check. The state beach access records were last updated between 2013 and 2019. Listings are active listings as of 2026-10-13.
- **Completeness (some entrances stated as all).** Myrtle Trace: back gate only. Prestwick: a main gate and a side gate. Bellwood Landing: a main gate and a delivery and construction entrance. Wachesaw East: a main gate and a card-key back gate. Litchfield by the Sea: three staffed gates, and guests at Willbrook Plantation, Reserve and Reunion Hall follow the host's instructions (row 5). Rows 1 to 3 cover unincorporated Horry County only: Prestwick, Bellwood Landing, Covington Lake East, Waterway Palms, The Bluffs and Indigo Bay are in it; Tidewater, Seaside, Barefoot and Grande Dunes are in a city.
- **Firmness (a listing field stated as a rule).** "Gated", "GatedCommunity", "guarded", "call box", "business card", "card key only" and the golf field are what seller's agents typed. Say "listings show", never "is". Row 22's card key line and row 30's buzz-in line each rest on one listing. HOA fees are seller-entered; $308 at The Bluffs is twice $154.

**Safety, crime and residents.** No row makes a safety, crime or resident claim, and none draws a conclusion about a named HOA or builder. Things to keep off the page: the words "secure", "exclusive", "luxury" and "upscale" in the Barefoot quotes; "protect our residents" in the Myrtle Trace quote (row 13); "Security" in a listing's HOA includes line; the surname in the Waterway Palms buzz-in quote (row 30 and its evidence table: delete it from the ledger); builder names in the price quotes (rows 44 to 50); the "55 and older" label unless taken from the batch 2026-10-a rows that verified it (rows 13, 14, 51, 76).

## Deciding fact (reported first)

The page needs at least 8 communities, in at least three areas, whose gate is shown by a source we can trust. **Count found: 21 communities in 7 areas:** North Myrtle Beach (Barefoot Resort, Seaside Plantation, Tidewater Plantation), Myrtle Beach (Grande Dunes, Prestwick), Carolina Forest (Covington Lake East, Waterway Palms Plantation, The Bluffs on the Waterway, Indigo Bay), Murrells Inlet (Seasons at Prince Creek West, Bellwood Landing, Wachesaw Plantation, Wachesaw East), Pawleys Island and Litchfield (Litchfield by the Sea, The Reserve, Heritage Plantation, Pawleys Plantation, Litchfield Plantation, Willbrook Plantation), DeBordieu Colony near Georgetown, and Conway (Myrtle Trace, back gate only). No gated community was found inside the Town of Surfside Beach; Prestwick is the closest (its nearest public beach access is in Surfside Beach, row 57).

By the strength of the source:

- **The association's own site or document (3):** Barefoot Resort, named neighborhoods only (rows 8 and 9); Litchfield by the Sea (rows 4 to 7); Myrtle Trace, back gate only (row 13, verified in batch 2026-10-a).
- **The builder's own page (1):** the Cascadia section of Grande Dunes, inside a "24-hours a day, staff-gated section" (row 11). Listings add which other Grande Dunes sections are gated (row 34).
- **A gate document recorded with the county, plus listings (2):** Seaside Plantation (rows 15 and 17) and Bellwood Landing (rows 16 and 18). The county shows only the index entry, so the rules themselves are not known.
- **Two allowed listing sites agreeing, marked as listings (15):** Seasons at Prince Creek West (row 14, verified in batch 2026-10-a), Prestwick, Tidewater Plantation, Wachesaw Plantation, Wachesaw East, The Reserve, Heritage Plantation, Pawleys Plantation, Litchfield Plantation, Willbrook Plantation, DeBordieu Colony, Covington Lake East, Waterway Palms Plantation, The Bluffs on the Waterway, Indigo Bay (rows 17 to 34).

Checked and **not** shown gated by listings: Wild Wing Plantation, Del Webb North Myrtle Beach, Plantation Lakes and Del Webb at Grande Dunes (rows 35 to 38).

## How to open the sources

- **Listing sites (marked as listings, never a primary source).** The Beach Pro Team, ERA Real Estate Modo, `https://www.beachproteam.com/listings/view/<address-slug>-sc-real-estate-<MLS#>.html` (robots.txt allows /listings/, asks for a 10-second crawl delay, which was honored), and RE/MAX Southern Shores, `https://mbcoastalhomes.realgeeks.com/property/<MLS#>/` (robots.txt names ClaudeBot and Claude-User under "Allow: /"). Both are fed by the Coastal Carolinas MLS. Each listing used is in the evidence tables at the end. "Gated on both sites" means the RE/MAX Southern Shores field "Amenities" includes "Gated" and the Beach Pro Team fields "Assoc Amenities" include "Gated" or "Security Features" include "GatedCommunity". The listing search used is `https://mbcoastalhomes.realgeeks.com/search/results/?city=all&neighborhood=<MLS neighborhood>&type=all&list_price_min=all&list_price_max=all&area_min=all&beds_min=all&baths_min=all`, which shows listings for sale on 2026-10-13. Never Zillow, Realtor.com or Redfin listing pages.
- **Register of Deeds (AcclaimWeb).** Open https://acclaimweb.horrycounty.org/AcclaimWeb/ and accept the conditions. A Book/Page opens at `https://acclaimweb.horrycounty.org/AcclaimWeb/details/JumpToBookPage/1/<book>/<page>`. The county posts the index entry, not the document text.
- **Sale prices, Horry County.** The method of batch 2026-10-a (seasons ledger row 73): every DEED (001) recorded 10/1/2025 to 9/30/2026 (AcclaimWeb search by Doc Type, month by month; 30,339 deeds countywide, the same total row 73 verified) whose index parcel number is one of the community's parcels in Horry County GIS layer 24 (`https://www.horrycounty.org/parcelapp/rest/services/HorryCountyGISApp/MapServer/24/query?where=<filter>&outFields=PIN,LegalDescr,LandUseCode&returnGeometry=false&f=json`, filter given in each row). Not counted: consideration under $10,000, corrective or re-recorded deeds, deeds on parcels the county codes as vacant land (land use 100), and deeds whose seller is a builder or company named in the row (reported apart). Quartiles use the inclusive method. A check: this code reproduces seasons ledger row 73 and myrtle-trace ledger row 81 exactly (19 sales, median $499,000; 35 sales, median $300,000).
- **Sale prices, Georgetown County.** AcclaimWeb covers Horry County only. For Georgetown County the county's own open data has a parcel table with the last sale on each parcel: `https://gis1.georgetowncountysc.org/portal/rest/services/GCGIS_OpenData/FeatureServer/7/query?where=<filter>&outFields=*&f=json` (layer "PARCELATTRIBUTES", fields SaleDate, SalePrice, LandUseCode, LegalDescription). It holds only the **last** sale of each parcel and no seller name, so a home sold twice counts once and builder sales cannot be taken out. Rows using it say so. Houses are land use codes ending in 100 or 101.
- **Drive times.** OSRM public router (OpenStreetMap roads), fastest route, no traffic. End points: S.C. Department of Environmental Services beach access layer, `https://gis.des.sc.gov/gisserver/rest/services/BeachAccess/MapServer/0/query?where=OBJECTID%3D<id>&outFields=*&returnGeometry=true&outSR=4326&f=json`, records with ACC_TYPE "PUBLIC BEACH ACCESS" or "BEACH PARK" and PARKING "Yes" (a car must be able to park). For each start, an OSRM table to the 40 nearest such accesses by straight line; the fastest kept, then routed alone. Minutes up to 10 are rounded to the nearest minute, over 10 to the nearest 5 (the rule used in batch 2026-10-a). **Start point:** the county address point nearest the average position of the community's home address points (Horry County Addresses layer 22, by the PINs in the price row), or for Georgetown County the home parcel nearest the average of the home parcel centers (layer 2, `https://gis1.georgetowncountysc.org/portal/rest/services/GCGIS_OpenData/FeatureServer/2`). Each row names its start address.
- **County code.** Horry County Code of Ordinances, Chapter 18 (Land Development Regulations), Municode, Supplement 88 (codified through Ordinance No. 37-2026, adopted June 16, 2026). Library page: `https://library.municode.com/sc/horry_county/codes/code_of_ordinances?nodeId=COOR_CH18LADERE`. The text was read through Municode's content service, `https://api.municode.com/CodesContent?jobId=494166&nodeId=COOR_CH18LADERE_ART4DEST_S2ST&productId=10129`.

## Fair housing and claims

No row says anything about safety, crime or who lives anywhere. Listing text that says "secure", "safe" or describes residents was not recorded. No row draws a conclusion about a named HOA or builder. Guard hours from listings are not recorded as fact (seasons ledger row 94 sets the rule).

ARITHMETIC: recomputed from the JSON: 33 sales, low $183,000, high $2,178,000, median $645,000, middle half $340,000 to $1,045,000. Correct. LISTINGS: opened all 33 (and the 5 in row 91) on mbcoastalhomes.realgeeks.com/property/<MLS#>/ (robots.txt allows Claude-User; /property/ is not disallowed; I did not open Zillow). Every price, closing date (all inside 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30), type and status CLOSED matches the JSON. All show Region 41a Pawleys Island Area-Litchfield Beaches and Amenities Gated. Neighborhood field names the section; 31 of 33 descriptions say Litchfield or LBTS; 2517518 and 2600059 (Summerhouse at LBTS) do not in the text but the MLS neighborhood is Summerhouse at LBTS. ARE THESE SECTIONS PART OF THE COMMUNITY: yes, all of them. The association's own site (litchfieldbythesea.com/communities/ and /community/, litchfieldbythesea.org is a parked page) lists 30 sub-associations. It names Bridgewater, Seaside Inn, Summerhouse, Lakeside, Sandpiper Run (its page covers Sandpiper Run and the Crescent), Somerset and Breakers Reef. Cambridge and Warwick are NOT separate sections: the Somerset page says Somerset has the buildings Fordham, Whitney Parrish, Warwick, Hamilton, Cambridge and Paget (listings 2513333 and 2610234 also say Somerset). So the nine MLS section names are seven association sub-associations. Do not write nine sections. Caveats: Seaside Inn is a hotel-style property (association: guest rooms and suites; the sale 2606829 is a condo with lockout), and Summerhouse is 98 one-bedroom units run with the resort; both are on the association list. MISSING SECTIONS (the sampling gap is real): I searched the MLS by the association's other section names and found 10 more whole-unit condo closings in the same window that the scan missed: Heron Marsh (5: 2508168 $540,000, 2511481 $595,000, 2523404 $600,000, 2605779 $610,000, 2606229 $610,000), Marsh Hawk (2: 2524029 $535,000, 2605250 $570,000), Fordham (2528976 $1,385,000), Hamilton (2518154 $1,050,000), Shipyard Village (2524131 $750,000). One more, Magnolia Run 2606637 $394,000, is a River Club golf villa whose text does not name Litchfield by the Sea, so I did not count it. The Paget and Whitney Parrish buildings returned nothing under the names I tried. With the 10 the count is 43 and the middle sale is $610,000 (middle half $513,500 to $1,022,500); the low and the high do not change. The pooled middle moves with which sections were found, and the pool is two groups (9 sales under $400,000, 10 at $1,000,000 or more), so a single middle figure is not safe. EXCLUDED SALES: spot-checked 2610727, 2500435, 2528694, 2614798, 2614067, 2522062, 2615776: all say interval or shared-week ownership. 2613816 and 2613853 (125 South Dunes, no description, fee $5,311) are unclear and stay out. A page that says condos sold from about $180,000 must say whole condos, because shared-week units sold from $19,500 to $220,000. SAFE WORDING (page may not say its condos as a whole): 'Whole-unit condos in the sections we counted sold for about $180,000 to $2.2 million between October 2025 and September 2026 [Coastal Carolinas MLS closed sales, 33 in 7 sections, with at least 10 more in other sections not in that count]'. The extremes are firm for what was found; the middle is not. If a middle is wanted: 'about $600,000 to $650,000 in the middle, in the sections we counted' is the most the data supports, and I would not use 'usually'. PAGE CHANGES: paragraph: replace 'Over the last 12 months, its condos sold for about $180,000 to $2.2 million.' with 'In the sections we counted, whole condos (not shared weeks) sold for about $180,000 to $2.2 million over the last 12 months.' Table cell: replace 'Condos about $180,000 to $2.2 million' with 'Condos in the sections we counted: about $180,000 to $2.2 million'. Do not use nine. |

WRONG: "Golf and the clay courts take a separate membership". The club's own site (prestwickcountryclub.com, 1001 Links Road): "Rated Top Public Course! ... has the look and feel of a private club, but is open to the public". Club + Resort Business (2016-02-16, the date is on the page): the owner "made the golf course solely a daily-fee course on December 31" and "was doing away with memberships". Public tee times are posted for 2026. So golf is a daily-fee course, not a membership. Five of the 17 listings (2620425, 2526904, 2602370, 2601394, 2528757) say golf is a separate or optional membership; they conflict with the club's site and are out of date. (Do not confuse with prestwickcc.com, an Illinois club.) STANDS: 18-hole Pete Dye course; large pool and smaller pool; 11 clay courts and 2 hard courts; clay courts need a tennis club membership (article, 2016; 8 listings 2026 say tennis or tennis stadium membership is separate). Listings 2622303 and 2620425 (2026) say residents have the pool; the article (2016) says the pool and the 2 hard courts are open to homeowners. CORRECT: "The owners association owns": the article says both "purchased" and a lease to a third-party operator; ownership today is not shown. Safe wording: "Prestwick has an 18-hole golf course between the homes, open to the public by the round [club site]. Its tennis center has clay courts and two hard courts, and it has a large pool and a smaller pool [Club + Resort Business, 2016; listings 2026]. The clay courts take a separate tennis membership [same]". Trade-off line: "the clay tennis courts cost extra, through a separate membership; golf is paid by the round". Researcher note: The article is undated on its page; it follows the club's 2015 announcement (linked from it). 2026 listings agree on the pool, the courts and separate memberships. |

| 129 | (added 2026-10-14, round 8) Willbrook: part of a 2,400-acre grant to Robert Daniel in 1711; by 1850, 140 enslaved people worked its rice fields; hurricanes from 1889 to 1911 broke the dikes and ended rice growing along the Waccamaw. Dan Maples' course opened in 1988 after an archaeological study; along it stand the chimney of the plantation house, which burned in 1895, and the cemetery of the enslaved people of Oatland Plantation. | as stated | myrtlebeachgolftrips.com (Myrtle Beach Golf Trips, the golf-package site of the area's golf marketing group) (two articles drawn from the course's history markers) | https://www.myrtlebeachgolftrips.com/news/five-historical-items-you-didnt-know-about-willbrook-plantation/ ; https://www.myrtlebeachgolftrips.com/news/willbrook-plantation-golf-club-celebrates-30-years-on-a-land-steeped-in-ric | "Willbrook was part of a 2,400-acre tract granted by the Lords Proprietors to Robert Daniel in 1711" "At the height of rice production in 1850, these cabins housed 140 slaves who toiled daily in the Willbrook rice fields" "the hurricanes of 1889, 1893, 1898, 1906, 1910, and 1911 wrecked the dike system and ended rice production along the Waccamaw River" "In 1988, Willbrook Plantation Golf Club was built on that land, but not until after extensive study" "There's a chimney that still stands at the site of the plantation house, a sign marking the slaves cemetery" "the original Willbrook Plantation house ... surviving until it burned in June 1895" "Oakland Plantation Slave Cemetery (8th hole) ... slaves who labored on Oatland Plantation". | 2026-10-14 | 2027-10 | wrong | 2026-10-14, round 8 independent verifier. WRONG on three numbers and one cause; the rest can stand. Primary source: Chicora Foundation Research Series 31, "Archaeological and historical examinations of three eighteenth and nineteenth century rice plantations on the Waccamaw Neck" (Trinkley, SC State Library), which cites the SC Archives and History 1850 Georgetown Slave Schedule. (1) GRANT: "originally part of a 24,000 acre tract granted by the Lords Proprietors to Landgrave Robert Daniel on June 18, 1711". The course markers (via two golf-package articles) say 2,400; 2,400 is the size of the Willbrook development area ("The 2400 acre Willbrook Plantation area"). (2) ENSLAVED PEOPLE: "In 1850, 149 slaves worked on 375 acres of improved farm land owned by Tucker" (Table 1: Willbrook 149). The marker says 140 housed in the cabins. 149 is the census count. (3) HURRICANES: Chicora lists "the hurricanes of 1893, 1894, 1898, 1906, 1910, and 1911 that wrecked the dike system"; the marker adds 1889. Chicora also names the loss of a stable work force and competition from western rice lands as causes. (4) HOUSE: "By 1895 the presumed original 1798 structure burned and was replaced the next year by a new house ... This 1896 structure remained intact until demolished in 1985." So the standing chimney is not from the house that burned in 1895. STANDS: the course opened in 1988 after an archaeological study (Chicora survey 1987; Memorandum of Agreement of July 23, 1987 for golf-course impacts; Golf Trips: "built in 1988"). The cemetery is from the course marker only (it is headed Oakland, its text says Oatland); Chicora's study does not describe it. Safe wording for the page, plain: "Willbrook was part of a 24,000-acre grant made by the Lords Proprietors to Robert Daniel in 1711. Rice was grown here by enslaved people. The 1850 census counted 149 enslaved people at Willbrook. After the Civil War, the loss of workers, rice grown farther west and hurricanes from 1893 to 1911 that wrecked the dikes ended rice growing on the Georgetown rivers." "Dan Maples' course opened in 1988, after an archaeological study of the land. A marked cemetery of enslaved people and the brick remains of the plantation house, rebuilt after a fire in 1895, are beside the course." Never as a selling point; keep it in the history paragraph. The owner may ask the photo partner for a photo of the cemetery marker. Researcher note: Designer: the course is a Dan Maples design (row 107 listings; Golf Trips "Maples' Dandy Dozen"). |
| 130 | (added 2026-10-14, round 8) Litchfield Plantation began with royal land grants to Thomas Hepworth from 1710 to 1712, and Peter Simons named it; it grew rice on the Waccamaw, and the state's survey of Georgetown County's rice plantations lists it. Its plantation house dates from the 1700s. | as stated | SC Department of Archives and History, SC Historic Property Record S108042003700044; Wikipedia (Litchfield Plantation) | https://schpr.sc.gov/index.php/Detail/objects/S108042003700044 ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Litchfield_Plantation | SCDAH record: "Litchfield Plantation", collection "Georgetown County - Rice Culture, 1974-1982". Wikipedia: "three land grants of 500, 500 and 420 acres from King George III to Thomas Hepworth, in 1710, 1712 and 1711. The plantation was named 'Litchfield' by Peter Simon[s]". House: Wikipedia 1740; the state record lists 1794; listings 1740 and 1750. | 2026-10-14 | 2027-10 | wrong | 2026-10-14, round 8 independent verifier. WRONG in part. SCDAH record S108042003700044 (quote): "Litchfield Plantation", "Street Address: Georgetown County", "Date Surveyed: 1982-05-18", "Construction Date: 1794", "Survey: Georgetown County - Rice Culture, 1974-1982". That supports: the state's Rice Culture survey lists it, and a house of the 1700s (the state says 1794; Wikipedia 1740; a listing 1750). NOT supported: the Hepworth grants and Peter Simons naming it rest on Wikipedia only, which says the grants came "from King George III" in 1710 to 1712, impossible (South Carolina was then under the Lords Proprietors, so not royal grants). Chicora Foundation (Research Series 31) only says Captain Thomas Hepworth owned land south of the 1711 Willbrook tract, and that Peter Simons is linked to Litchfield by a 1791 plat but "no records were found of any land holdings on the Waccamaw Neck" for him. Chicora also says the Tucker family consolidated Willbrook and Litchfield. Safe wording: "Litchfield was a rice plantation on the Waccamaw River; the state's Rice Culture survey of Georgetown County lists it [SC Archives and History]. Its plantation house dates from the 1700s. In the 1800s it belonged to the Tucker family, who also owned Willbrook [Chicora Foundation]." Researcher note: "Peter Simons": Wikipedia spells it Simon and Simons in different places. The page says "the 1700s" for the house because the dates differ. |

WRONG as sourced: secondary source. Wikipedia (The Litchfield Company) is tagged as needing references and cites none. The company's own profile (LeadingRE, thelitchfieldcompany.com returned 403) says only "Since 1956, The Litchfield Company Real Estate has dedicated itself to serving ... the communities along the South Carolina coast", which is the brokerage, not who built Litchfield by the Sea. Closest primary evidence: Chicora Foundation Research Series 31 (1990) says the study "was funded by The Litchfield Company of South Carolina", which was advancing the Willbrook golf course in 1987, and that title to part of the land passed to "Litchfield by the Sea" in 1984. That shows the company developed Willbrook, not that it built Litchfield by the Sea or was founded in 1956. Comes off the page: "The Litchfield Company, founded in 1956, built Litchfield by the Sea". Safe wording: "Litchfield by the Sea lies between the marsh and the ocean." Ask the owner for the Georgetown County recorded declaration if the developer is wanted. Researcher note: Secondary source; a county plat or a Georgetown Times article would be stronger. |

I drew them and the 396 Heritage parcels (Georgetown layers 7 and 2, legal description HERITAGE PLANT) over the 2023 NAIP aerial: the mapped creek runs from the Waccamaw River along the marsh at the north edge of the Heritage tract, and the tract's outline takes in that marsh; the houses lie south and east of it. A short-term permit lets a truck park in a set area of the clubhouse lot. | vote 5-0; cycle ends 2033 | Myrtle Trace HOA, News and Views, October 2026 (pages 1 and 5) | https://myrtletracesc.org/wp-content/uploads/News-Views/NV2026/2026-10-Oct-NV.pdf | "A previous Board established a guideline permitting short-term truck parking, with a permit, in a designated area of the clubhouse parking lot." / "the original restrictions remain in effect for twenty years from their recording in 1983 and automatically renew for successive ten-year periods" / "the Board voted unanimously (5-0) not to pursue a modification of the covenants at this time. Quotes found on p1 and p5: covenant bars trucks on the Properties (Art. VII s.17); a previous Board's guideline allows a short-term permit in a designated area of the clubhouse lot; "the Board voted unanimously (5-0) not to pursue a modification of the covenants at this time. The current ten-year amendment cycle ends in 2033." The renewal arithmetic holds (1983 + 20 = 2003, then 2013, 2023, 2033). Page: "the board has decided not to seek a change before the covenants renew in 2033" says more than the source ("at this time"; the board says 2033 is the appropriate time for residents to consider it). Safe wording: In 2026 the board voted 5 to 0 not to pursue a change now; the current ten-year period ends in 2033 [newsletter, October 2026]. Consistent with batch a row 71 (that row is marked wrong; this one is later). Struck in struck-v2.json. | 293 | (added 2026-10-14, round 14) Prestwick: when the Jackson Companies ended club memberships at the end of 2015, it offered the tennis and swim facilities to the owners association for $1 each. The association took them over: 11 clay courts and 2 hard courts, a tennis pro shop, lockers, a pavilion, a half Olympic-size pool and a smaller pool. | $1 each; 13 courts; 2 pools | Club + Resort Business, 2015-10-12, 2015-12-15 and 2016-02-16 | https://clubandresortbusiness.com/prestwick-cc-transitions-to-daily-fee-golf-course/ ; https://clubandresortbusiness.com/prestwick-cc-poa-keeps-tennis-swim-facilities-going/ | 2015: "it has offered to lease or convey those amenities to the community's Property Owners Association for $1 each so they can remain in operation at the discretion of the POA". 2016: "The POA purchased the facilities, which include 11 clay courts and two hard courts, a tennis pro shop, locker facilities, a pavilion with restrooms, a half Olympic-size swimming pool and a smaller pool" | 2016-02-16 | 2027-04 | wrong | 2026-10-15, round 14 independent verifier. Secondary source: Club + Resort Business rewrites Myrtle Beach Online ("Online reported"); the primary article or the POA/Jackson letter was not found by search. The row also merges two reports that disagree. 2015 (Oct 12): the owner "offered to lease or convey" the amenities to the POA for $1 each; it lists 11 clay and two hard courts, a pro shop, lockers and a half Olympic-size pool only. 2016 (Feb 16): the lede says lease for $1 each, then "The POA purchased the facilities", then the POA president says "we ended up putting together a lease agreement with a third-party operator" (Jimmy Mendieta, Prestwick Tennis Club), the "pool facility and the two hard courts are now available to Prestwick's more than 600 homeowners" and the 11 clay courts need the tennis club's membership. Page: "the owners association took over the large pool, a smaller pool and the tennis center ... The clay courts need a tennis membership of their own" is present tense from a 2016 report whose purchase/lease terms conflict, and the operator reportedly moved on by 2017 (researcher's notes). Correct statement: in 2015 the owner offered to lease or convey the tennis and swim facilities to the association for $1 each; a 2016 report lists 11 clay courts, two hard courts, a pro shop, lockers, a pavilion and two pools. Whether the association owns or leases them, and what is open today, is not verified. Cut the sentence or date it to 2016. Struck in struck-v2.json. Both are nine years old and call the grill East Grill and Pub; the club's site now has the Toasted Tee Pub & Grub at 911 Riverwood Drive. County (Georgetown) 2026: the course, lakes and wetlands are in the name of WACHESAW GOLF LLC, mailing address 1 Vance Gap Rd, Asheville; no source says that LLC is Festiva's. CORRECT: say Festiva Real Estate Holdings bought the course and its grill in 2017, and the course is part of the Ellington at Wachesaw Plantation East resort [Club + Resort Business, 2017]; do not say vacation ownership or timeshare, and do not say belong in the present tense without a 2026 source. Struck list: gated 334, 335 (v9). |

Chicora RS11 PDF p.59 matches the Freedmen's Bureau quote (seized 1865, worked until December 1865, profits divided). MAIN PROBLEM: RS11 says the 2,400-acre Willbrook DEVELOPMENT (Willbrook, Oatland and Turkey Hill) is the land of three plantations (abstract, PDF p.5; the 1985 plan was 50 holes scattered over the tract). The course's own About page says the course is 'Winding through a pair of plantations'. No source puts the 18-hole course on all three. | 393 | (added 2026-10-14, round 14) DeBordieu's owners pay for their own beach. As a gated community it does not qualify for public renourishment money, so in 2017 the owners voted to create a beach preservation fund, paid by assessments and expected to raise up to $12 million over 17 years. Sand was pumped onto the beach in 2015 (795,000 cubic yards), and in 2021 a court cleared a project of three rock and concrete groins and up to 650,000 cubic yards of sand on 1.5 miles at the south end, where a seawall stands and the beach was passable only part of the day. | up to $12 million over 17 years; 795,000 cu yd (2015); 650,000 cu yd and 3 groins (2021) | DCCA Beach Preservation page; Coastal Observer, January 21, 2021 and October 1, 2021 | https://www.debordieucolony.org/public-resources/beach-preservation/ ; https://coastalobserver.com/judge-upholds-state-permit-for-debordieu-groins/ ; https://coastalobserver.com/ruling-clears-way-for-debordieu-to-start-beach-project/ | DCCA: "On March 18, 2017 during a Special Meeting of Members your community voted to amend the By-Laws of the DeBordieu Colony Community Association to establish a fund for beach preservation on Debidue Beach." ; Jan 2021: "As a gated community, DeBordieu doesn't qualify for public funds for beach renourishment." "pumping 795,000 cubic yards of sand onto the beach in 2015" ; Oct 2021: "place up to 650,000 cubic yards of offshore sand on 1.5 miles of beach at the south end of the community. The work includes the installation of groins to hold the sand." "a beach fund through assessments on property owners. Over 17 years, it is expected to generate up to $12 million." "the beach in front of an existing seawall is impassible for about half the day" | 2021-10-01 | 2027-04 | verified with corrected wording | 2026-10-15, round 14 independent verifier. Beach Preservation page opened: 'On March 18, 2017 during a Special Meeting of Members your community voted to amend the By-Laws ... to establish a fund for beach preservation'. Coastal Observer Jan 21, 2021 opened: 'As a gated community, DeBordieu doesn't qualify for public funds for beach renourishment'; '795,000 cubic yards of sand onto the beach in 2015'; permit for three rock and concrete groins and up to 650,000 cubic yards on 1.5 miles; judge upheld the permit. Oct 1, 2021: 'a beach fund through assessments on property owners. Over 17 years, it is expected to generate up to $12 million'; stay denied; the Coastal Conservation League's appeal to the Court of Appeals was pending; 'impassible for about half the day'. I found no report that the groins were built or on the appeal's result. What the page may state: DeBordieu, a gated community, does not qualify for public renourishment money [Coastal Observer, 2021: one reporter's statement about DeBordieu, no statute found]; in 2017 the owners voted to set up a beach preservation fund [DCCA]; the fund is paid by assessments [Coastal Observer]; sand was placed in 2015; a state judge upheld the permit for a groin project in 2021. It may not say 'a gated community cannot get public money' (a general rule), or that the 2017 vote was made because of that (no source gives a reason). Say 'a court cleared', not 'built'. Redid it two ways. (a) County GIS layer 19 (Flood Zones; it holds only the non-X polygons): layer 24 gives 193 parcels LegalDescr LIKE 'COVINGTON LAKE EAST%'; the place's bbox meets one AE polygon (OBJECTID 1018) and one 0.2 PCT polygon (968); server-side intersect of each against the 193 parcels: 0 touch. Six random lots, whole-lot and centre tests against layer 19: nothing. (b) FEMA's own NFHL answered (hazards.fema.gov/arcgis/rest/services/public/NFHL/MapServer/28): all 193 parcel polygons intersect only FLD_ZONE X, ZONE_SUBTY "AREA OF MINIMAL FLOOD HAZARD" (SFHA_TF F, panel series 45051C); five lot-centre points the same. WORDING: Zone X (minimal) is itself a FEMA zone, so "no lot touches a FEMA flood zone" is wrong in letter; and "even with its ponds" is the writer's aside. FEDERAL RULE: 42 U.S.C. 4012a(b) directs regulated lenders not to make or renew a loan secured by improved real estate in an area the Administrator has identified as having special flood hazards (the Special Flood Hazard Area: A and V zones) unless it is insured; shaded X and unshaded X are outside it. A lender or a buyer can still choose insurance; a flood can happen outside the mapped zone; and a new map or a map revision can change a lot. Safe wording: "On FEMA's current map every lot is in Zone X, minimal flood hazard; none is in a high-risk zone (the Special Flood Hazard Area) or the shaded moderate zone. The federal rule that makes a lender require flood insurance applies to homes in the high-risk zones, so it does not apply to any home here by the current map [FEMA National Flood Hazard Layer, read 2026-10-15]. Ask us to check any address." Do not write "no risk" or "will never need". Struck list: struck-v7.json. |

## Waiting for MLS

- Sale prices for the Georgetown County communities from closed MLS sales (the county table keeps only each home's last sale and no seller name, rows 52 to 56).
- Typical prices for Willbrook Plantation, Litchfield Plantation, Wachesaw Plantation, Litchfield by the Sea and Oak Pointe (see Not verified).
- Days on market and price per square foot in gated communities against the area.
- HOA fees from closed sales, not only homes for sale on 2026-10-13. The fee rows are what sellers entered on current listings.

## Search check

Searches read 2026-10-13: "gated communities in Myrtle Beach SC" and "55+ gated communities Myrtle Beach" (finders only, never sources).

| # | Result | What it answers | What it does not answer |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | homeguidemyrtlebeach.com, "Gated Communities in Myrtle Beach" | A list of names with links to listings | Fees, what homes sell for, what kind of gate, which part is gated |
| 2 | mbcoastalhomes.realgeeks.com/gated-communities/ | A listing search page | Anything from a record |
| 3 | countryclubmag.com, "Top 20 Most Expensive Gated Communities" | A ranked list of names | Sources, fees, gate kind |
| 4 | resident.com, "Why Gated Communities in Myrtle Beach Are Perfect for Retirees" | General claims, including security and insurance claims we may not make | Anything verifiable |
| 5 | Agent pages on 55+ communities | Names Carillon at Tuscany, Beachwood at the Heritage and Del Webb sections as gated | No source; row 38 found no gate on 19 Del Webb at Grande Dunes listings |

What a buyer asks that none of them answers: which communities are gated by a record or the builder, and which only in part (Barefoot, Grande Dunes, Myrtle Trace); what a home in each sold for in the last 12 months by the county's deed records; the HOA fee per community; minutes to a public beach access; who maintains the roads behind a gate (rows 1 to 4); how guests, contractors and deliveries get in (rows 5 to 7).

## Not verified

- **Gate kind** for Seaside Plantation, Covington Lake East, The Reserve and Indigo Bay: no source says whether there is a guard, a call box or an arm only. Grande Dunes: only the Cascadia section is tied by its builder to the staffed gate (row 11); the Grande Dunes Master Association's own site (a TownSq portal, grandedunescommunities.sites.townsq.io) was found but not read, and no association document saying which sections are behind which gate was found.
- **Guard hours** from listings were not recorded (seasons row 94 rule). Prestwick and Tidewater listings call their gates guarded; when the guard is there is not shown. Litchfield by the Sea is the only community with published hours (row 6).
- **Deliveries.** Only Litchfield by the Sea publishes a rule for commercial vehicles (row 7). No source read says how parcel carriers get through any other gate. Bellwood Landing listings mention a separate delivery and construction entrance (row 18).
- **Private roads in the cities.** Rows 1 to 3 are Horry County rules for developments under the county's land development regulations. Barefoot Resort, Tidewater Plantation, Seaside Plantation and Grande Dunes are inside a city by their listings' "Lot Location" ("In City Limits"); the City of North Myrtle Beach and City of Myrtle Beach rules were not read. Georgetown County's rule was not read (its Municode client lookup returned nothing). Whether each community's streets are in fact private was not checked road by road; the page can say "gated streets are usually private roads the HOA maintains" only with that limit.
- **Emergency access through gates** (fire code rules on gates across fire apparatus roads) was not researched.
- **55+ status.** Only Myrtle Trace and Seasons at Prince Creek West are known 55+ (batch 2026-10-a). No age rule was read for any other community, so the data file leaves 55+ empty for them.
- **Prices not given:**
  - Willbrook Plantation: Georgetown County's open data server reset every connection late on 2026-10-13 (tried four times).
  - Litchfield Plantation: county legal descriptions name only 22 houses (50 parcels), clearly not all of it; 2 sales.
  - Wachesaw Plantation: most of its parcels do not carry the name in the county table (the 51 that do are its Wachesaw Farms section; 3 sales).
  - Litchfield by the Sea: many sections under other names; not attempted.
  - Oak Pointe (Barefoot): no county legal description names it.
  - Cascadia (Grande Dunes): no home resale in the window (row 12).
- **Beach minutes not given:** Litchfield by the Sea (oceanfront with its own beach club; the main gate point at US 17 and Willbrook Boulevard could not be geocoded: Nominatim returned nothing). Seaside Plantation's figure (row 59) is to a city access 0.6 miles away; it is not a statement that Seaside has its own beach access.
- **Leads not checked:** Carillon at Tuscany (55+), Beachwood at the Heritage, Hunt Club at Hunters Ridge, Waterway Hills (no MLS neighborhood of that name found on the listing site), Kingston Plantation and Myrtle Beach Resort (oceanfront condo resorts; a rental company's page, visitmbr.com, gives Myrtle Beach Resort gate fees, which is not a primary source), the Waterside Pointe section of Del Webb at Grande Dunes (that ledger's note 5: a recorded rule set and a declaration clause allowing "private gate access" for Parcel C).
- **Georgetown County sale table.** Its latest SaleDate is 2026-12-29, a date in the future, so some dates in it are wrong; sales dated after 2026-09-30 were not used. The verifier should re-run one parcel against the county's deed records (georgetowndeeds.com) before the page uses rows 52 to 56.
- **Gate documents in the deed index.** A comment search of AcclaimWeb for gate words found only Seaside Plantation (rows 15) and Bellwood Landing (row 16). A search on "GATE" alone returns nothing (the index search fails on that word), so others may exist.

## Questions only the brokerage can answer

1. For each gated community you show often: is the gate staffed, a call box or a code, and at what hours? Do agents get in with a business card, a code from the listing agent, or a call to the seller?
2. How do packages and food deliveries get in at Prestwick, Tidewater, Wachesaw and the Carolina Forest gated neighborhoods (Covington Lake East, Waterway Palms, The Bluffs)?
3. Which sections of Grande Dunes are behind the staffed gate at the bridge, and which have only their own gate? Is Del Webb's Waterside Pointe gated?
4. Do buyers who ask for "gated" usually mean a staffed guardhouse, or any gate?
5. From your own closings: typical HOA fees and sale prices in Litchfield Plantation, Willbrook Plantation and Wachesaw Plantation, where the county records were incomplete.
